name: Kabelwerk Rhönsberg GmbH
summary: Kabelwerk Rhönsberg is a group-owned cable maker founded in 1957, with about 400 staff and EUR 98.1 M turnover. Its finances are stable: equity ratio 32.3 % and credit index 149, unchanged from 12 months ago. It is our single source for motor cable part:350040, but we are only 0.8 % of its turnover. Our framework agreement expires on 2026-12-31. The supplier has asked for our volumes and quoted an unchanged price of 316.35/100, saying its copper is bought forward until March 2027.

situation.decision_maker: Key account manager can agree price changes up to 2 %. Anything above 2 % needs the group pricing committee, which meets every two weeks (doc:20260415-70560-M2).

negotiation_pattern: It opens with an annual increase and gives back about 2.3 points: mean asked 4.47 %, mean settled 2.2 %. Past renewals: 2023 asked 2.1 %, settled -1.0 %. 2024 asked 2.7 %, settled 1.6 %. 2025 asked 8.6 %, settled 6.0 % (EV-2026-70560-350040), which went through the pricing committee. Between renewals the price moves quarterly via the copper index clause (EV-2026-70560-350040-Q3). The supplier is process-driven: moves above 2 % are slow and need committee approval. It defends its hedged copper position ('market price is not our reality').
wants: volume forecast and visibility for 2027 (it explicitly asked for expected volumes)
renewal of the framework, ideally longer term, to secure an A-category customer
price stability matching its copper hedge until March 2027
on-time payment (we pay late in 73 % of cases)
keeping deals within the key account manager's 2 % authority, to avoid the committee cycle
protects: unit_price: list/committee policy; already only about 3.9 % above the no-margin should-cost
index_clause logic: it will resist index-driven decreases while its copper is hedged until March 2027
payment_days: no reason to go beyond 30 net, given our late-payment record

trades.give: contract_months up to 24 plus binding 2027 volume forecast (about 290k units/yr)
trades.get: unit_price fixed at or below 316.35 through at least 2027-03-31 (end of its copper cover), within the 2 % band
trades.why: Its material cost is locked until March 2027, so a firm price costs it nothing. A longer term secures our business.

trades.give: commitment to pay strictly on due date (fix our 73 % late share)
trades.get: payment_days 45, as a term concession rather than a price concession
trades.why: A group moves on terms more easily than on list price. Our late payment is a sore point we can turn into currency.

trades.give: keep the CU-NOTATION index clause after March 2027
trades.get: no index increases before April 2027, and a new index base set at contract start
trades.why: It says market copper is not its reality until March 2027. It cannot ask for index upside on hedged material.

trades.get: OTD improvement plan towards the contractual 95 %, plus ppm_commitment ≤100
trades.why: OTD has been 81.5–88.9 %, well below the 95 % target.

arguments.point: Your own quote says material is covered until March 2027. A firm price through that date carries no risk for you.
Our spend has grown every year (EUR 740k → 813k → 834k). We can give you a 2027 forecast in exchange for price stability.
Last renewal we accepted +6.0 %. This year we expect stability.
Delivery performance of 88.5 % OTD is below the contractual 95 % target. A longer agreement must come with a delivery improvement.
Keep the proposal within 2 % so your key account manager can sign without waiting for the pricing committee.

avoid: Demanding cuts above 2 % up front: this triggers the pricing committee, delays the deal and hardens positions.
Presenting the should-cost (+3.9 %) as hard fact: estimate confidence is only 5 %, and the margin is already thin.
Arguing with current copper market prices before March 2027: it has declared its hedge 'not our reality'.
Threatening to switch supplier without a qualified alternative: there are zero other sources, and we are only 0.8 % of its turnover.
Pushing longer payment terms without addressing our own late payments.
tone: Professional, structured and data-based. Give clear, approvable proposals within the key account manager's 2 % authority, framed as a long-term partnership with forecast security.
red_flags: Deadline: price-change notice and termination notice both fall 60 days before 2026-12-31, i.e. by about 2026-11-01. Otherwise the contract auto-extends 12 months.
Single source with 100 % quota and no other sources for an A-part. Our dependency is real, theirs on us is minimal (0.8 %).
OTD persistently below the 95 % target (81.5–88.9 %). Supply risk if volume grows.
Risk of an index increase in 2027 after the copper hedge expires.
Our late-payment record (73 % late) weakens our leverage on terms.

evidence.claim: Price changes above 2 % need approval of the pricing committee, which meets every two weeks.
Copper is bought forward until March 2027. The supplier calls market price 'not our reality'.
New quote holds the price flat at 316.35/100, 14 days lead time, 30 days payment.
Framework expires 2026-12-31, auto-extends 12 months, 60 days' notice. Price changes need 60 days' notice before year end.
Price follows CU-NOTATION quarterly with 55 % material share and no deadband.
Price is only 3.9 % above the no-margin should-cost (estimate confidence 5 %).
OTD 88.5 % vs 95 % target. ppm 111. Scorecard green, class A. No open 8D.
Supplier asked for our expected volumes for the renewal.

indicators.credit_index: 149 (12 months ago 149; higher is worse, >300 weak)
